info.title: Modjo Public API
info.description:
The Modjo Public API lets you programmatically access your Modjo workspace data — calls, users, teams, and webhooks.

### Base URL

```
https://api.modjo.ai//v2
```

### Getting Started

1. [Create an API key](#tag/Authentication) from your Modjo settings.
2. Include it as a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header of every request.
3. Browse the endpoints below to list calls, manage users, configure webhooks, and more.

### Pagination

All list endpoints return paginated results. Use the `page` (1-based, default: 1) and `size` (default: 25, max: 100) query parameters to navigate through results. Every paginated response includes a `pagination` object with `page`, `size`, and `total` fields.

### Expanding Relations

Some endpoints support a `expand` query parameter that lets you inline related objects instead of receiving only their IDs. Pass a comma-separated list of fields (e.g. `?expand=contacts,deal`). When a relation is expanded, the corresponding ID field is omitted from the response.

### Need Help?

Contact your Modjo account manager or reach out to [support@modjo.ai](mailto:support@modjo.ai).

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description:
Modjo API authentication is based on an API key that must be included in the request headers.

To authenticate, add your API key to the `Authorization` header as a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

### How to Retrieve Your API Key

Before generating a new API key, you must have **Administrator** or **Manager** permissions.

Follow these steps to create your API key:

1. **[Log in to Modjo](https://app.modjo.ai)**
2. **[Go to Settings](https://app.modjo.ai/settings/?utm_source=api-doc)**
3. **[Access the Integrations section](https://app.modjo.ai/settings/integrations?utm_source=api-doc)**
4. **[Find the Public API card](https://app.modjo.ai/settings/integrations/modjo_api_key?utm_source=api-doc)**
5. Create a new API key.

Make sure to keep your API key **secure** and do not share it with unauthorized parties.

### Rate Limiting

The API enforces a rate limit of **100 requests per minute** per API key. Rate limit information is included in response headers:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: Maximum number of requests allowed per window
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: Number of requests remaining in the current window
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: Seconds until the rate limit resets

If you exceed the rate limit, you will receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response.

tags.name: Errors
tags.description:
The API uses conventional HTTP status codes and returns a consistent JSON error body.

### Error Response Format

```json
{
  "code": "not_found",
  "message": "Call not found"
}
```

### Error Codes

| HTTP Status | Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `validation_error` | The request body or query parameters are invalid. The `message` field describes which fields failed validation. |
| 401 | `missing_api_key` | No `Authorization` header was provided. |
| 401 | `invalid_api_key` | The API key is invalid, revoked, or the tenant has been deleted. |
| 404 | `not_found` | The requested resource does not exist. |
| 409 | `conflict` | The resource already exists (e.g. duplicate email or webhook name). |
| 410 | `gone` | The resource existed but has been permanently deleted (e.g. a recording removed by data retention policy). |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | You have exceeded the rate limit. Wait and retry after the `X-RateLimit-Reset` interval. |
| 500 | `internal_error` | An unexpected error occurred on our side. If this persists, contact support. |

tags.name: Calls
tags.description:
A call represents a recorded conversation in Modjo (phone call, video meeting, etc.).

### Call Statuses

| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| `processing` | The call has been received and is being downloaded, transcribed, or analyzed. |
| `completed` | The call is fully processed and the transcript is available. |
| `failed` | Processing failed (e.g. empty recording, damaged file, no speakers detected). |

### Uploading Calls

Use `POST /calls` to upload a call via a publicly accessible recording URL. The call is processed asynchronously — you will receive a UUID immediately and can poll `GET /calls/{id}` until the status changes from `processing` to `completed` or `failed`. Typical processing time is 5 to 30 minutes.

### Expanding Relations

The list and get endpoints support the `expand` query parameter with the following fields:
- **contacts** — inline contact details instead of `contactIds`
- **deal** — inline deal details instead of `dealId`
- **account** — inline account details instead of `accountId`
- **users** — inline user details instead of `userIds`

### Downloading Recordings

Use `GET /calls/{id}/recording` to retrieve a signed URL to download the call recording media file. The URL is valid for 1 hour; request a new one once it expires. The recording is only available while the call `recordingRetentionStatus` is `available`.

tags.name: Call Reviews
tags.description: Call reviews are structured evaluations of a call filled in against a review template. Each review carries an overall rating, per-question answers with individual ratings, and metadata (reviewer, reviewee, whether it was with the help of an AI agent). Use this endpoint to export call reviews.

tags.name: CRM Filling Answers
tags.description: CRM filling answers represent values that have been pushed to a CRM after a call was processed. Each answer is linked to a specific call and a CRM filling field. Only answers that have been successfully pushed to the CRM are returned.

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description: Contacts represent external people associated with your calls and deals (e.g. prospects, customers). Use these endpoints to list and search contacts in your workspace.

tags.name: CRM Filling Templates
tags.description: CRM filling templates define how Modjo automatically fills CRM fields after calls. Each template specifies the language, call duration filters, applicable providers, and which teams and tags it applies to. Templates can be in `pending` (draft) or `published` (active) status.

tags.name: Deals
tags.description: Deals represent sales opportunities tracked in your CRM. Use these endpoints to list deals and retrieve AI-generated deal summaries.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description: Tags are labels that can be applied to calls for categorization and filtering. Use this endpoint to list available tags in your workspace.

tags.name: Topics
tags.description: Topics represent conversation subjects detected in calls (e.g. pricing, competitors). Topics can be grouped into categories. Use this endpoint to list available topics in your workspace.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Users represent licensed members of your Modjo workspace. Each user has a unique email address within the tenant. Use these endpoints to list, create, update, or deactivate users, and to manage their team membership programmatically.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description: Teams let you group users together for organizational purposes (e.g. "Sales", "Customer Success"). Use these endpoints to manage teams and their membership.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Webhooks let you receive real-time notifications when events occur in your Modjo workspace.

### Supported events

| Event | Description |
|---|---|
| `call_created` | Fired when a call has been imported and created in Modjo. |
| `call_summarized` | Fired when a call has been fully processed and its summary is available. |
| `call_recording_deleted` | Fired when a call recording has been deleted. |
| `call_tag_added` | Fired when a tag is added to a call. |
| `call_tag_removed` | Fired when a tag is removed from a call. |
| `call_transcribed` | Fired when a call transcription is complete. |
| `call_transcript_deleted` | Fired when a call transcript has been deleted. |

### Delivery format

When an event fires, Modjo sends a `POST` request to your webhook URL with this JSON body, here for a `call_tag_added` event:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2024-06-15T14:30:00.000Z",
  "payloadSignature": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08",
  "webhookUuid": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "webhookUrl": "https://example.com/webhooks/modjo",
  "tenantName": "acme",
  "eventName": "call_tag_added",
  "payload": {
    "callId": 12345,
    "title": "Discovery call - Acme",
    "startDate": "2024-06-15T14:00:00.000Z",
    "duration": 1820,
    "provider": "zoom",
    "providerCallId": "8912345678",
    "language": "en",
    "callCrmId": "00Q5g00000ABCDeEAF",
    "relations": {
      "tag": {
        "tagId": 42,
        "tagName": "Pricing objection"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `timestamp` | string | ISO 8601 date the signature was computed with. Same value as the `x-modjo-timestamp` header. |
| `payloadSignature` | string | Signature of the payload. Same value as the `x-modjo-payload-signature` header. |
| `webhookUuid` | string | UUID of the webhook the delivery was sent to. |
| `webhookUrl` | string | URL the delivery was sent to. |
| `tenantName` | string | Name of your Modjo workspace. |
| `eventName` | string | One of the supported events listed above. |
| `payload` | object | Event-specific data. See [Event payloads](#event-payloads). |

Modjo waits up to 30 seconds for your endpoint to respond before treating the delivery as failed.

### Verifying deliveries

Every delivery carries two headers:

| Header | Description |
|---|---|
| `x-modjo-payload-signature` | Hex-encoded SHA-256 signature of the payload. |
| `x-modjo-timestamp` | ISO 8601 date used to compute the signature. |

The signature is:

```
sha256( x-modjo-timestamp + JSON.stringify(payload) + secretToken )
```

hex-encoded. Two points matter:

- the signed material is the `payload` object alone, not the full request body;
- the timestamp is the value from the header (equal to the body's `timestamp`), not your own clock.

```js
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';

const expected = createHash('sha256')
  .update(`${body.timestamp}${JSON.stringify(body.payload)}${secretToken}`)
  .digest('hex');

const isValid = expected === request.headers['x-modjo-payload-signature'];
```

If your JSON serializer may order keys or escape characters differently from ours, sign the raw `payload` substring of the request body instead of re-serializing the parsed object.

The secret token is displayed once, in Settings > Integrations > Webhook, when the webhook is created. It is never returned by an API response and never sent in a delivery. See the [help center article](https://help.modjo.ai/en/articles/10470126-webhooks).

### Event payloads

#### Call payload

Sent by `call_created`, `call_transcribed`, `call_recording_deleted` and `call_transcript_deleted`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `callId` | integer | Modjo identifier of the call. |
| `title` | string | Call name. |
| `startDate` | string \| null | Call start in ISO 8601, `null` if unknown. |
| `duration` | integer | Duration in seconds, `0` when unknown. |
| `provider` | string | Telephony or meeting provider of the call. |
| `providerCallId` | string | Call identifier at the provider. |
| `language` | string \| null | Transcript language, `null` if undetermined. |
| `callCrmId` | string \| null | CRM activity identifier linked to the call. |

#### Tag events

`call_tag_added` and `call_tag_removed` send the eight call fields above plus a `relations.tag` object. The Delivery format example above shows a complete `call_tag_added` delivery.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `relations.tag.tagId` | integer | Modjo identifier of the tag. |
| `relations.tag.tagName` | string | Label of the tag as it appears in Modjo. |

The tag is read at `payload.relations.tag.tagId` and `payload.relations.tag.tagName`.

#### `call_summarized`

The call fields above except `providerCallId`, which this event does not send, plus `relations.activity`, `relations.summary`, `relations.contacts` and `relations.callUsers`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `callId` | integer | Unique identifier of the call. |
| `title` | string | Name of the call. |
| `startDate` | string \| null | Start date of the call in ISO 8601 format. |
| `duration` | integer | Duration of the call in seconds. |
| `provider` | string | The telephony provider used for the call. |
| `language` | string \| null | Language of the call transcript. Can be null if language is unknown. |
| `callCrmId` | string \| null | CRM activity ID linked to the call. |
| `relations.activity.activityCrmId` | string \| null | Unique identifier of the CRM activity associated with the call. |
| `relations.activity.activityCrmType` | string \| null | Type of CRM activity: `calendarEvent` when the call is linked to a calendar event that could be found, `call` otherwise. Meeting providers such as Google, Microsoft or Zoom generally have a calendar event; phone providers default to `call`. |
| `relations.activity.crmDealId` | string \| null | CRM deal ID associated with the call activity. Can be null if not available. |
| `relations.activity.crmAccountId` | string \| null | CRM account ID associated with the call activity. Can be null if not available. |
| `relations.summary.content` | string \| null | Summary content generated for the call. |
| `relations.summary.templateUuid` | string | UUID of the summary template used. |
| `relations.summary.summaryCrmId` | string \| null | CRM note ID where the summary was stored. |
| `relations.contacts[].contactId` | integer | Unique identifier of the contact. |
| `relations.contacts[].contactCrmId` | string \| null | CRM person ID linked to the contact. Can be null if not available. |
| `relations.contacts[].contactCrmType` | string | CRM entity type for the contact (e.g. "Lead" or "Contact"). |
| `relations.contacts[].contactEmail` | string \| null | Email address of the contact. Can be null if not available. |
| `relations.contacts[].contactPhoneNumber` | string \| null | Phone number of the contact. Can be null if not available. |
| `relations.callUsers[].userId` | integer | Internal unique identifier for the system user who participated in the call. |
| `relations.callUsers[].userEmail` | string | Email address of the system user, used for identification and communication. |

```json
{
  "callId": 12345,
  "title": "Discovery call - Acme",
  "startDate": "2024-06-15T14:00:00.000Z",
  "duration": 1820,
  "provider": "zoom",
  "language": "en",
  "callCrmId": "00Q5g00000ABCDeEAF",
  "relations": {
    "activity": {
      "activityCrmId": "00T5g00000XYZabEAF",
      "activityCrmType": "calendarEvent",
      "crmDealId": "0065g00000DEFghEAF",
      "crmAccountId": "0015g00000JKLmnEAF"
    },
    "summary": {
      "content": "The prospect is evaluating three vendors and needs pricing by Friday.",
      "templateUuid": "3f2504e0-4f89-11d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301",
      "summaryCrmId": "0065g00000NOPqrEAF"
    },
    "contacts": [
      {
        "contactId": 987,
        "contactCrmId": "0035g00000STUvwEAF",
        "contactCrmType": "Contact",
        "contactEmail": "jane.doe@acme.com",
        "contactPhoneNumber": "+33123456789"
      }
    ],
    "callUsers": [
      {
        "userId": 42,
        "userEmail": "sales.rep@yourcompany.com"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

For every event, if the referenced call or tag can no longer be read when the event is processed, no request is sent for that event.

### Delivery failures

A non-2xx response or a timeout is retried 4 times, so an event is attempted 5 times in total. After the fifth failed attempt the webhook is marked `down` and receives no further events until a Modjo operator reactivates it. If deliveries stop after an outage on your side, contact Modjo support to have the webhook reactivated.
